Sounds interesting. The latest update to ChatGPT adds Mac integration, allowing it to handle conversations in Apple's "Messages" app. This feature supports iMessage, SMS, and RCS.

ChatGPT for Mac now has a new Apple "Messages" plugin

This brand-new Apple "Messages" plugin lets ChatGPT read and search conversation histories on your Mac, as well as prepare and send messages. OpenAI says this feature is available on all plans for the macOS version of the ChatGPT desktop app, and also supports ChatGPT Work and Codex.

This level of access inevitably raises concerns about privacy and control, so OpenAI emphasises that sending messages still requires user approval by default. Users should think carefully before granting persistent approval. OpenAI's plugin guidelines detail the relevant risks, how to revoke permissions, and a known issue involving a workflow that disables approval prompts.

For now, this feature only works on Macs with Apple Silicon; Intel models are not yet supported.

If you ask ChatGPT to send a message for you, a confirmation prompt will pop up before any message is sent. You can also choose to skip the confirmation step in individual conversations.

Want to find this new feature in ChatGPT? This link should take you directly to the "Messages" plugin in the Mac version of ChatGPT.

Collaborative website editing, conversation snapshot sharing, and more

Although the "Messages" plugin is the most eye-catching new feature for Apple users, this update also includes several other improvements. For example, pinned conversations can now sync between the ChatGPT desktop app and iOS, so users can browse important conversations on both Mac and iPhone at any time.

ChatGPT can now also let users share read-only snapshots of local Codex conversations. These snapshots will not change as the original conversation updates.

Links created from personal accounts can be accessed by anyone with the URL; however, workspace links remain accessible only to members of that workspace. OpenAI says Codex masks known sensitive data patterns, but reminds users to review snapshots themselves, as sensitive information may still be present.

In addition, website owners can invite active members of the same workspace to collaboratively edit sites that support collaboration. Editors can update content and database information, save versions, and publish changes after the owner completes the initial launch. The owner retains final control over access, settings, analytics, and version rollback.

Some website owners can also change the URL hosted by ChatGPT without redeploying; the old URL will automatically redirect to the new URL.

Finally, the "Computer Use History" feature launched last week will be expanded to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK. This optional feature requires enabling "Memories" and is off by default.

You can see the full release announcement for this update here.
